app.customerDeleteConsequence_one: {{count}} project will also be deleted. Servers are kept but will no longer be assigned to a customer.
app.customerDeleteConsequence_other: {{count}} projects will also be deleted. Servers are kept but will no longer be assigned to a customer.
app.customerDeleteServersKept: The customer’s servers are kept but will no longer be assigned to a customer.
app.serverDeleteConsequence_one: {{count}} project is kept but will no longer be assigned to a server.
app.serverDeleteConsequence_other: {{count}} projects are kept but will no longer be assigned to a server.

welcome.title: Welcome to Hostmoor
welcome.text: Get started by adding your first customer or server.

app.selectHint: Select a customer, project, or server in the sidebar.

restore.title: Restore backup?
restore.description: All current customers, servers, and projects will be replaced with the contents of <file>{{file}}</file>. Export a backup first if you want to keep your current data.

sidebar.empty: Nothing here yet. Use <icon/> to add your first customer or server.

resizer.label: Sidebar width
resizer.title: Drag to resize, double-click to reset

entityDialog.customerDescription: Customers group projects and servers together.
entityDialog.serverDescription: Connection details for the SSH check. Passwords are never stored.
entityDialog.projectDescription: A customer’s website or app, e.g. a Laravel shop.
entityDialog.assignTo: Will be assigned to the project “{{name}}” after saving.

project.pathHint: Will be used for deploy scripts.
project.repoHint: Used to show GitHub or GitLab Actions.

server.sshKeyHint: Only the path is stored. The app never opens the key file; it’s only passed to ssh -i. Leave empty to use the default key or the SSH agent.
server.proxyJumpHint: Only if the server can only be reached through another host. Passed to ssh -J; a name from ~/.ssh/config works too. Leave empty for a direct connection.

detail.noData: No data for this server yet. Click “{{action}}” and Hostmoor reads PHP, Node, capacity and more. Nothing on the server is changed.

panel.title: Connection
panel.intro: Checks whether this computer can sign in to this server via SSH. Nothing on the server is changed.
panel.selfRun: You run these commands yourself in Terminal. Hostmoor doesn’t change anything on the server.

button.openTitleInDir: Open SSH session in {{app}}, directly in {{dir}}

sshHelp.confirmHost: Connect once yourself in Terminal and answer “Are you sure you want to continue connecting?” with yes. Then you can close the connection with exit.

ok.title: Connected
ok.explanation: Signing in as {{user}} works. The server is ready for the server check.
ok.explanationNoUser: Signing in with your user works. The server is ready for the server check.

unknownHost.title: Server is not known yet
unknownHost.explanation: This computer has never connected to this server. So that no one can impersonate your server, the app doesn’t confirm new servers automatically.

hostKeyChanged.title: Warning: The server key has changed
hostKeyChanged.explanation: This happens when the server was reinstalled. But it can also mean that someone is impersonating your server. Only continue if you’re sure the server was set up again.
hostKeyChanged.removeEntry: Only if you’re sure: remove the old entry.

authFailed.title: Key not accepted
authFailed.explanation: The server is reachable, but signing in as {{user}} fails. Usually the public key isn’t on the server yet.
authFailed.explanationNoUser: The server is reachable, but signing in with your user fails. Usually the public key isn’t on the server yet.
authFailed.noUser: No SSH user is set. Enter the correct one in the server form, e.g. root, deploy or forge.
authFailed.generateKey: Create a dedicated key for this server. It’s saved to {{key}} and also works normally in Terminal afterwards. If you already have a key you want to use, enter its path in the server form instead.
authFailed.useKey: Use this key for the server:
authFailed.copyId: Copy the public key to the server. This asks for the server password once:
authFailed.pbcopy: Can’t sign in with a password? Copy the public key to the clipboard and paste it into your host’s panel (or Forge, Plesk …) under “SSH keys”:
authFailed.passphrase: Does your key have a passphrase? The app can’t ask for it. Store it once in the macOS keychain:
authFailed.showPublicKey: Can’t sign in with a password? Show the public key, copy it and paste it into your host’s panel (or Forge, Plesk …) under “SSH keys”:
authFailed.passphraseAgent: Does your key have a passphrase? The app can’t ask for it. Add the key to the running SSH agent once:

keyNotFound.title: Key file not found
keyNotFound.explanation: There’s no file at {{key}}. Check the path in the server form or create a new key.
keyNotFound.generateKey: Or create a new key at exactly this path:
keyNotFound.copyAndRetry: Then copy the public key to the server and test again.

keyPermissions.title: Key file is readable by others
keyPermissions.explanation: For security reasons, ssh won’t use the key as long as other users could read it.

dnsFailed.title: Host not found
dnsFailed.explanation: The name “{{host}}” can’t be resolved. Check the spelling or enter the IP address directly.

refused.title: Connection refused
refused.explanation: The server responds, but SSH isn’t running on port {{port}}. Often the port is wrong (default: 22) or SSH isn’t enabled on the server.

timeout.title: No response from server
timeout.explanation: No response within 8 seconds. Common causes: wrong IP, the server is off, or a firewall (e.g. in the Hetzner panel) is blocking port {{port}}.

unreachable.title: Server unreachable
unreachable.explanation: The network can’t find a route to the server. Are you on the right network or VPN, and is the IP correct?

invalidConfig.title: Check your input
invalidConfig.explanation: Host or user contains characters that aren’t allowed. Please correct them in the server form.

unknown.title: Connection failed
unknown.explanation: The cause couldn’t be detected automatically. The message from ssh is shown in the details below.
unknown.verbose: Try it yourself in Terminal to see what happens:

detail.notChecked: This server hasn't been checked yet.
detail.noServer: No server is assigned to this project yet.

panel.repoUrlNotRecognized: Couldn't recognize the repo URL “{{url}}”. Use a format like git@github.com:company/project.git or https://gitlab.com/group/project.
panel.noRepoUrl: Add a repo URL to the project to see its latest runs here.
panel.tokenRejected: The saved token for {{host}} was rejected or has no access to this repo.
panel.tokenMissing: This repo is private or unreachable. Add a token for {{host}} so Hostmoor can read its runs.

token.title: Token for {{host}}
token.description: The token is stored in the {{store}}, not in the Hostmoor database or in backups. It applies to all projects on {{host}}.
token.helpGithub: Recommended: a fine-grained token with “Actions: Read-only” access to the repos you need. If an organization owns the repo, select it as the resource owner, and make sure the token isn't pending approval. A classic token with the repo scope also works, but grants much broader access.
token.helpGitlab: Create a personal access token on {{host}} with the read_api scope. That's all Hostmoor needs.
token.placeholderReplace: Paste a new token to replace the current one

panel.missingServer: Assign a server to this project first.
panel.missingPath: Add the project's path on the server (e.g. /var/www/shop). The script runs there.
panel.editorHelp: Runs with bash in {{path}} on the server. Each command is shown, and the deploy stops at the first error. Lines starting with # are comments.
panel.noScript: No deploy script yet. Define which commands run on the server when you deploy, for example git pull and composer install.
panel.confirmDescription: These commands will run on {{server}} ({{target}}) in {{path}}:

api.importBrowserOnly: Importing only works in the app, not in the browser.
api.connectionTestBrowserOnly: The connection test only works in the app, not in the browser.
api.deployBrowserOnly: Deploys only work in the app, not in the browser.
api.ciBrowserOnly: Pipelines can only be loaded in the app, not in the browser.
api.terminalBrowserOnly: The terminal can only be opened from the app, not from the browser.
api.serverCheckBrowserOnly: The server check only works in the app, not in the browser.
api.siteBrowserOnly: Certificates can only be checked in the app, not in the browser.
api.logsBrowserOnly: Logs can only be read in the app, not in the browser.
api.sshConfigBrowserOnly: The SSH config can only be read in the app, not in the browser.

update.title: Hostmoor {{version}} is available
update.description: You are using version {{current}}. The update is downloaded and installed, then Hostmoor restarts.
update.browserOnly: Updates are only available in the desktop app

site.title: SSL & domain
site.noDomain: Add a domain to the project to watch its SSL certificate.
site.autoCheck: Checked every 6 hours. You get a notification 14 and 3 days before expiry.

logs.title: Logs
logs.clearDescription: All entries in the file are deleted on the server. This can't be undone.
logs.missingServer: Assign a server to the project to read its logs.
logs.missingPath: Add the project's path on the server; relative log paths start there.
logs.noPaths: No log files yet. Add the paths of the logs you want to read.
logs.pathsHelp: One file per line. Relative paths start in the project folder {{path}}, absolute ones like /var/log/nginx/error.log need read access for the SSH user.
logs.footer: Shows the last {{count}} lines. Errors and warnings are counted in the whole file, every 30 minutes and on “Refresh”.

sshImport.title: Import servers from SSH config
sshImport.description: Hostmoor reads ~/.ssh/config and the files it includes. The file is never changed, and key files are not opened.
